title: Why Advanced Chip Packaging Is Becoming a Design Problem - Semiwiki
gist: A TSMC talk at the 2026 OIP Forum argues advanced multi-die packaging has become a co-design problem spanning layout, signal integrity, power delivery and thermals, citing AI-assisted chiplet placement fixes, minutes-scale automated routing, and power simulations cut from over a month to days.

insights.claim: In advanced packaging, physical layout, electrical performance, heat and mechanical structure now have to be considered together, changing the tools used to design chips.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Raises demand for multi-physics EDA and packaging design tools.

insights.claim: Progress in computing increasingly depends on making many components work as one system, so gains will come from coordinating manufacturing technology and design tools across the whole package.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Favors players spanning foundry, packaging and EDA ecosystems.
insights.quote: advanced packaging needs an equally advanced design process

insights.claim: Misaligned grids between through-silicon connections, wiring tracks and standard-cell sites can waste space; TSMC adjusts connection placement to recover cell area, gaining capacity without a new manufacturing process.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Small area recoveries at scale translate into cost-per-function gains without node migration.

insights.claim: TSMC describes an AI system that examines remaining chiplet placement rule violations and proposes fixes, such as changing which edges line up rather than pushing chiplets apart.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-assisted packaging layout reduces manual rework as packages become more crowded.

insights.claim: TSMC reports automated tools routed large groups of high-speed signals in minutes where manual work would take much longer, though these are talk-reported results rather than guarantees for every design.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Productivity gains in packaging design could shorten time-to-market for chiplet products.

insights.claim: A statistical method described by TSMC makes it practical to estimate very rare bit-error rates in die-to-die links that direct simulation cannot reach in reasonable time.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Faster signal-integrity sign-off allows more design exploration before commitment.

insights.claim: TSMC is moving voltage conversion closer to compute chips so power travels farther at higher voltage and lower current, reducing losses but adding components that must be modeled.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Points to growth in integrated voltage regulation and package-level power delivery content.

insights.claim: Simplified, layered power-delivery models have reduced simulations that once took more than a month to a matter of days, according to the TSMC speaker.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Order-of-magnitude simulation speedups shorten package design cycles.
insights.quote: reduced simulations that once took more than a month to a matter of days

insights.claim: Thermal models that spread heat evenly across a circuit cell can miss hot spots, so TSMC is developing more detailed thermal models for new power structures, metal wiring and optical components whose behavior changes with heat.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Thermal accuracy becomes critical as co-packaged optics enter packages.

insights.claim: A packaging technology is only useful if engineers have reliable rules, models and software; TSMC found capacity, runtime and accuracy issues when testing these with tool partners.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Design-enablement readiness, not just process capability, gates advanced packaging revenue ramps.
insights.quote: A promising packaging technology is only useful if engineers have reliable rules, models, and software to design with it.
